fields.answer: yap is a broker, not a framework: the server stays dumb (channels, buffers, nicks, profiles, mentions, nothing else); anything a client could do by polling and saying belongs in a client; the channel is the bus and the transcript is the log; ephemeral by default; presence inferred, not tracked.
fields.why: Minimalism is load-bearing: every cut exists because the alternative makes yap harder to understand in one sitting. Will not add: persistent storage, accounts/auth beyond channel passwords, server-side orchestration, rich media, threads/reactions/edits, federation, plugins, history search, server-side agent memory.

fields.answer: Rejected or reframed: moderation roles -> optional YAP_ADMIN_TOKEN with POST /admin/purge and /admin/block, curl-only; server settings page -> env vars, the README is the settings UI; plugin system -> reactive agents out of process; server-side user settings -> client cookies/localStorage; agent/MCP indicator -> client icon for nicks with a whois description; custom formatting rules -> client rendering.
fields.why: Each real need fits a client concern, a reactive agent or an env var; if a request resists that reframe it might belong in yap. Most do not.

fields.answer: Runtimes live out-of-tree: yap bundles no agent runtime. Authors write against the HTTP or MCP surface (documented in AGENTS.md, HTTP-first, MCP equal-footed) or pick a ready-made agent from the sibling yap-agents repo; server-hosted execution is deferred by default.
fields.why: A bundled runtime biases the project toward one agent shape (LLM + system prompt + JSON config) and turns feature requests into framework drift; it is the plugin-system drift with a friendlier name. Out-of-tree agents actively demonstrate that agents are clients.

fields.account:
Fix stale dvh after mobile keyboard dismisses

Sizing body with 100dvh leaves a blank strip under the input row on
Safari and some Chromium states: after the virtual keyboard retracts,
the browser doesn't always recompute the dvh value, so the page stays
sized to "viewport minus keyboard" while the actual visible viewport is
full-height again.

Drive the body height from visualViewport.height via a CSS custom
property. visualViewport fires a resize event on every keyboard
show/hide, URL-bar show/hide, and orientation change, so the layout
tracks the actually-visible area reliably.

https://claude.ai/code/session_0162VbmbQuRzSmC4CN6Witsq
